title: Father, How Wide Thy Glory Shines
description: Father, How Wide Thy Glory Shines in Tonic Solfa to ST. PETER, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 7 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words. John Wesley printed them in A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780), hymn 263.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Common Metre (8.6.8.6), and this page sets them to ST. PETER; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Fa-ther, how wide thy glo-ry shines! How high thy won-ders rise! Known through the earth by thou-sand signs By thou-sands through the skies.

lines: Father, how wide thy glory shines!
Known through the earth by thousand signs
Those mighty orbs proclaim thy power,
And on the wings of every hour
Part of thy name divinely stands
They show the labour of thy hands,
But when we view thy strange design
Here the whole Deity is known,
Which of the glories brightest shone,
Now the full glories of the Lamb
O may I bear some humble part
Wonder and joy shall tune my heart,

source: John Wesley, A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain, as printed in John Wesley's Collection of Hymns (1780); set to ST. PETER by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
